versions.source: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual 8th Edition / NCCN / UICC
versions.provenance: 8th edition staging, verified against AJCC 8th edition / NCCN guidelines; licensed verification standard. Requires R1 clinical verification before unchecked use.
versions.introduction: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumours (NETs) of the pancreas and gastrointestinal tract share WHO grading by Ki-67 proliferation index and mitotic count (G1: Ki-67 below 3 percent; G2: 3-20 percent; G3: above 20 percent well-differentiated), while poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs, small/large cell) are high-grade by definition and staged by the corresponding exocrine scheme. Pancreatic NET T reflects size and invasion (confined, duodenal/bile-duct invasion, major vascular or adjacent-organ invasion); GI NET T reflects depth of wall invasion and size. Functioning syndromes (insulinoma, gastrinoma, VIPoma, carcinoid) guide management but not stage.

t.label: Tumour limited to organ of origin: PanNET below 2 cm confined to pancreas; GI NET invading mucosa/submucosa and 1 cm or smaller
PanNET 2-4 cm confined to pancreas, or invasion of duodenum/bile duct; GI NET invading muscularis propria or larger than 1 cm up to 2 cm
PanNET larger than 4 cm, or invasion of duodenum/bile duct/peripancreatic tissues; GI NET invading through muscularis into subserosa or larger than 2 cm
Tumour invades adjacent organs or major vessels (coeliac axis, SMA): PanNET T4 requires arterial encasement or organ invasion; GI NET perforates serosa or invades neighbours

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Regional lymph node metastasis present (PanNET: any positive node; small-bowel NET schemes count mesenteric nodal masses)

m.label: Metastasis to extrahepatic site(s), with or without liver involvement
Both hepatic and extrahepatic metastases (pancreatic scheme)

stageGroups.basis: Any nodal metastasis without distant spread

versions.regionalNodes: Pancreatic: peripancreatic, pyloric, hepatic-artery and splenic-hilar nodes. Small bowel: mesenteric nodes (bulky mesenteric masses recorded). Colorectal: pericolic/perirectal and intermediate nodes. Distant liver, bone and lung deposits are M1.
versions.histologicGrade: WHO grade by Ki-67 index and mitotic count per 2 sq mm: G1 (Ki-67 below 3 percent, mitoses below 2), G2 (Ki-67 3-20 percent, mitoses 2-20), G3 well-differentiated NET (Ki-67 above 20 percent, mitoses above 20, retained differentiation); poorly differentiated NEC (small/large cell) is high-grade by definition.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Well-differentiated NET G1/G2/G3 (insulinoma, gastrinoma, glucagonoma, VIPoma, somatostatinoma, non-functioning); poorly differentiated NEC (small-cell, large-cell); mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasm (MiNEN); appendiceal, rectal and gastric type-specific variants.
